*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/generate_options.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+DATA = "data/crashes.parquet"
+years = list(range(2013, 2026))
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           sum(number_of_motorist_killed)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths,
+           sum(number_of_cyclist_killed)::BIGINT AS cyclist_deaths,
+           count(*) FILTER (
+               WHERE crash_date IS NULL
+                  OR number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL
+                  OR number_of_cyclist_killed IS NULL
+           ) AS rows_with_nulls
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchdf()
+
+assert annual["year"].tolist() == years
+assert annual["rows_with_nulls"].sum() == 0
+annual = annual.drop(columns="rows_with_nulls")
+annual["year"] = annual["year"].astype(int)
+annual["combined_deaths"] = annual["motorist_deaths"] + annual["cyclist_deaths"]
+annual["cyclist_share_pct"] = (
+    100 * annual["cyclist_deaths"] / annual["combined_deaths"]
+)
+
+counts = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT count(*) AS total,
+           count(*) FILTER (
+               WHERE crash_date IS NULL
+                  OR crash_date < DATE '2013-01-01'
+                  OR crash_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
+           ) AS excluded
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchone()
+excluded_share = 100 * counts[1] / counts[0]
+coverage = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, min(crash_date) AS first_date,
+           max(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchdf()
+assert all(str(row.first_date) == f"{int(row.year)}-01-01" for row in coverage.itertuples())
+assert all(str(row.last_date) == f"{int(row.year)}-12-31" for row in coverage.itertuples())
+
+# Option 1: compare annual fatality totals directly.
+annual[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths"]].to_csv(
+    OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False
+)
+x = np.arange(len(annual))
+width = 0.38
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
+ax.bar(x - width / 2, annual["motorist_deaths"], width, label="Motorist deaths", color="#3366a8")
+ax.bar(x + width / 2, annual["cyclist_deaths"], width, label="Cyclist deaths", color="#e07a35")
+ax.set_xticks(x, annual["year"])
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("NYC motorist and cyclist deaths by year (2013–2025)")
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 2: compare cyclist-vs-motorist composition among these two groups.
+annual[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths", "combined_deaths", "cyclist_share_pct"]].to_csv(
+    OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.2f"
+)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
+ax.bar(annual["year"], 100 - annual["cyclist_share_pct"], label="Motorist deaths", color="#3366a8")
+ax.bar(
+    annual["year"], annual["cyclist_share_pct"],
+    bottom=100 - annual["cyclist_share_pct"], label="Cyclist deaths", color="#e07a35"
+)
+ax.set_xticks(annual["year"])
+ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
+ax.set_ylabel("Share of motorist + cyclist deaths (%)")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("Share of motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC (2013–2025)")
+ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+motorist_peak = annual.loc[annual["motorist_deaths"].idxmax()]
+cyclist_peak = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_deaths"].idxmax()]
+share_min = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_share_pct"].idxmin()]
+share_max = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_share_pct"].idxmax()]
+excluded_note = (
+    f"The 2013–2025 filter excludes {counts[1]:,} of {counts[0]:,} file rows "
+    f"({excluded_share:.2f}%), those outside that range, including partial 2012 and 2026; "
+    "all included years are complete calendar years and no in-range rows have NULL dates or death counts."
+)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual sum of deaths by road-user group",
+            "denominator": "None; annual death counts",
+            "grouping": "Year, with motorist and cyclist as series",
+            "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart",
+            "reason": "Direct annual counts make the absolute difference between the two road-user groups easy to compare.",
+            "probability": 0.65,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in all 13 years; motorist deaths peaked at "
+                f"{int(motorist_peak.motorist_deaths)} in {int(motorist_peak.year)}, while cyclist deaths peaked at "
+                f"{int(cyclist_peak.cyclist_deaths)} in {int(cyclist_peak.year)}."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the annual numbers of motorist and cyclist deaths compare in absolute terms. "
+                "It shows motorist deaths were higher in each of the 13 years, with the peaks given in the answer. "
+                "Raw totals are a direct comparison of deaths, but do not adjust for travel exposure or explain causes. "
+                + excluded_note
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Cyclist deaths as a percentage of motorist plus cyclist deaths",
+            "denominator": "Motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths in the same year",
+            "grouping": "Year, split by motorist and cyclist",
+            "chart_type": "100% stacked bar chart",
+            "reason": "The within-year share emphasizes how the balance between these two categories changes independently of their combined total.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Cyclists accounted for {share_min.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% to {share_max.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% of motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, "
+                f"lowest in {int(share_min.year)} and highest in {int(share_max.year)}; motorist deaths made up the balance."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the relative mix of motorist and cyclist deaths changes year by year. "
+                f"Cyclist deaths made up {share_min.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}%–{share_max.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% of deaths in these two groups, "
+                "with the smallest and largest shares in the years stated in the answer. "
+                "This share is a defensible comparison of composition, but leaves the absolute annual death totals unanswered. "
+                + excluded_note
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print("Annual values:")
+print(annual.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Excluded rows: {counts[1]}/{counts[0]} ({excluded_share:.4f}%)")
+print("Cyclist share min/max:", share_min.to_dict(), share_max.to_dict())
*** End Patch

@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+DATA = "data/crashes.parquet"
+years = list(range(2013, 2026))
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           sum(number_of_motorist_killed)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths,
+           sum(number_of_cyclist_killed)::BIGINT AS cyclist_deaths,
+           count(*) FILTER (
+               WHERE crash_date IS NULL
+                  OR number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL
+                  OR number_of_cyclist_killed IS NULL
+           ) AS rows_with_nulls
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchdf()
+
+assert annual["year"].tolist() == years
+assert annual["rows_with_nulls"].sum() == 0
+annual = annual.drop(columns="rows_with_nulls")
+annual["year"] = annual["year"].astype(int)
+annual["combined_deaths"] = annual["motorist_deaths"] + annual["cyclist_deaths"]
+annual["cyclist_share_pct"] = (
+    100 * annual["cyclist_deaths"] / annual["combined_deaths"]
+)
+
+counts = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT count(*) AS total,
+           count(*) FILTER (
+               WHERE crash_date IS NULL
+                  OR crash_date < DATE '2013-01-01'
+                  OR crash_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
+           ) AS excluded
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchone()
+excluded_share = 100 * counts[1] / counts[0]
+coverage = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, min(crash_date) AS first_date,
+           max(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).fetchdf()
+assert all(str(row.first_date) == f"{int(row.year)}-01-01" for row in coverage.itertuples())
+assert all(str(row.last_date) == f"{int(row.year)}-12-31" for row in coverage.itertuples())
+
+# Option 1: compare annual fatality totals directly.
+annual[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths"]].to_csv(
+    OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False
+)
+x = np.arange(len(annual))
+width = 0.38
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
+ax.bar(x - width / 2, annual["motorist_deaths"], width, label="Motorist deaths", color="#3366a8")
+ax.bar(x + width / 2, annual["cyclist_deaths"], width, label="Cyclist deaths", color="#e07a35")
+ax.set_xticks(x, annual["year"])
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("NYC motorist and cyclist deaths by year (2013–2025)")
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 2: compare cyclist-vs-motorist composition among these two groups.
+annual[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths", "combined_deaths", "cyclist_share_pct"]].to_csv(
+    OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.2f"
+)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
+ax.bar(annual["year"], 100 - annual["cyclist_share_pct"], label="Motorist deaths", color="#3366a8")
+ax.bar(
+    annual["year"], annual["cyclist_share_pct"],
+    bottom=100 - annual["cyclist_share_pct"], label="Cyclist deaths", color="#e07a35"
+)
+ax.set_xticks(annual["year"])
+ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
+ax.set_ylabel("Share of motorist + cyclist deaths (%)")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("Share of motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC (2013–2025)")
+ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+motorist_peak = annual.loc[annual["motorist_deaths"].idxmax()]
+cyclist_peak = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_deaths"].idxmax()]
+share_min = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_share_pct"].idxmin()]
+share_max = annual.loc[annual["cyclist_share_pct"].idxmax()]
+excluded_note = (
+    f"The 2013–2025 filter excludes {counts[1]:,} of {counts[0]:,} file rows "
+    f"({excluded_share:.2f}%), those outside that range, including partial 2012 and 2026; "
+    "all included years are complete calendar years and no in-range rows have NULL dates or death counts."
+)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual sum of deaths by road-user group",
+            "denominator": "None; annual death counts",
+            "grouping": "Year, with motorist and cyclist as series",
+            "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart",
+            "reason": "Direct annual counts make the absolute difference between the two road-user groups easy to compare.",
+            "probability": 0.65,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in all 13 years; motorist deaths peaked at "
+                f"{int(motorist_peak.motorist_deaths)} in {int(motorist_peak.year)}, while cyclist deaths peaked at "
+                f"{int(cyclist_peak.cyclist_deaths)} in {int(cyclist_peak.year)}."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the annual numbers of motorist and cyclist deaths compare in absolute terms. "
+                "It shows motorist deaths were higher in each of the 13 years, with the peaks given in the answer. "
+                "Raw totals are a direct comparison of deaths, but do not adjust for travel exposure or explain causes. "
+                + excluded_note
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Cyclist deaths as a percentage of motorist plus cyclist deaths",
+            "denominator": "Motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths in the same year",
+            "grouping": "Year, split by motorist and cyclist",
+            "chart_type": "100% stacked bar chart",
+            "reason": "The within-year share emphasizes how the balance between these two categories changes independently of their combined total.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Cyclists accounted for {share_min.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% to {share_max.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% of motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, "
+                f"lowest in {int(share_min.year)} and highest in {int(share_max.year)}; motorist deaths made up the balance."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the relative mix of motorist and cyclist deaths changes year by year. "
+                f"Cyclist deaths made up {share_min.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}%–{share_max.cyclist_share_pct:.1f}% of deaths in these two groups, "
+                "with the smallest and largest shares in the years stated in the answer. "
+                "This share is a defensible comparison of composition, but leaves the absolute annual death totals unanswered. "
+                + excluded_note
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print("Annual values:")
+print(annual.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Excluded rows: {counts[1]}/{counts[0]} ({excluded_share:.4f}%)")
+print("Cyclist share min/max:", share_min.to_dict(), share_max.to_dict())
